Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches. This is a REWORK round on SFCC-91 Step 3, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/`. Do not stage, do not commit. Do not touch any file outside this one folder.

This component already passed an automated Scorer PASS, but Marcel then looked at it in a real running Storybook and found two real defects the automated pipeline could not see. Both are confirmed, not hypothetical — read the diagnosis below, it's already been traced to root cause.

## Fix 1 — a Storybook interaction test is polluting the "at rest" reference story

Read `index.stories.tsx` in full. `Default`'s `play` function currently does:
```tsx
selected.focus();
await expect(selected).toHaveFocus();
await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
await expect(canvas.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Ivory' })).toHaveFocus();
await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}');
await expect(selected).toHaveFocus();
```
This runs automatically every time the story mounts (Storybook always executes `play` on render), and it ends with a real swatch element holding real DOM focus. Because `Default` is the primary story a developer opens to visually judge "what does this look like at rest," a play function that leaves something focused makes the component look broken — a visible focus ring appears on load, disappears when the user clicks elsewhere (real focus moving away, expected), and does not return without a hard refresh (nothing re-runs `play` without a full remount). The component itself is behaving correctly; the story is testing the wrong thing in the wrong place.

**Fix:** move the arrow-key roving-focus assertions out of `Default` entirely, into a new, separate, clearly-named story dedicated to interaction testing — e.g. `KeyboardNavigation`. Check `index.test.tsx` first: this repo's `testing.md` says not to duplicate coverage across layers, so if the *non-focus* assertions currently in `Default`'s play function (the radio count, the `aria-checked` check) are already covered by an existing Vitest test, `Default` may not need a play function at all — judge this yourself by reading `index.test.tsx`, don't assume either way. Whatever you decide `Default` keeps, it must end in a state with nothing keyboard-focused, and ideally should not manipulate focus at all. The new `KeyboardNavigation` story (or whatever you name it) carries the arrow-key assertions instead, using the same fixture shape as `Default` if convenient.

## Fix 2 — the whole component visibly resizes when paging (real layout bug, not a design ambiguity)

Read `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` and `index.tsx` together. Root cause: `root` (`display:flex, flexDirection:column, gap:...`) has no explicit width, so its rendered width auto-fits to its widest child. `swatches` (`display:flex, width:100%, gap:0`) resolves that `100%` against whatever `root`'s auto-computed width currently is — which itself depends on how many swatch children are actually rendered right now. On the `Paginated` story's first page (4 populated colours visible, 4×48=192px of intrinsic content) `root` computes wide; after clicking "next" (only 2 remaining colours on the final page, 2×48=96px) `root` computes narrow. Since the `label` row is ALSO `width:100%` of that same shrinking `root`, the entire label-and-chevron row visibly reflows and repositions between pages — confirmed by Marcel directly in a running Storybook (screenshots showed the chevrons jump from far-right to right-next-to-the-label between the two pages of the same `Paginated` story).

**Fix:** when `isPaginated` is true, the swatches row (and therefore the whole component, since `root`'s auto-width follows its widest child) must maintain a STABLE width regardless of which page — including a partial final page — is currently showing. A paginated instance's width should always reserve room for a full `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` (4) swatches, i.e. `calc(4 * var(--zimm-scale-1200))` (192px, using the same token the atom already uses for a single swatch's 48px width) — a partial final page (e.g. 2 items) should occupy that same reserved footprint, with the unused space simply remaining empty to the right, rather than the container shrinking to fit only the real items. This is a reasonable, common pagination pattern and there is no Figma spec contradicting it for the partial-last-page case.

Do this the same way Step 2's sibling atom (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`) already handles a state-dependent style: make this recipe's `baseStyle` a function of `{ isPaginated }: { isPaginated?: boolean }` instead of the current plain object, and apply the stabilizing width/minWidth only inside the `isPaginated` branch. Wire it through by changing `index.tsx`'s `useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_COLOUR_SWATCH_GROUP_RECIPE, {})` to pass `{ isPaginated }` (the `isPaginated` value already exists in the component, computed from `populated.length > SWATCHES_PER_PAGE`).

**Explicitly out of scope — do not change this:** the non-paginated case (1-4 populated colours, no pagination controls) should keep sizing naturally to however many swatches are actually present. Nothing was reported broken about a 2- or 3-colour non-paginated product's row width, and there's no confirmed design value either way for that case — don't invent a fixed width for it.

**Known, accepted gap, do not try to fix it:** `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s automated fuzzing harness will not vary `isPaginated` (its `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS` only contains a fixed set of keys, same situation Step 2's `selected` prop hit) — so that guard won't walk the paginated branch. This is expected and matches an already-accepted pattern from Step 2's build; do not attempt to modify `recipeGuards.test.ts` to fix it, that file is out of this step's scope entirely.

**Required verification, empirical not just read:** add a Vitest test (or extend an existing one) in `index.test.tsx` that renders the paginated scenario (more than 4 populated colours), captures the swatches container's rendered width (e.g. via `getBoundingClientRect().width` or a `getComputedStyle` read on the relevant element — check which is reliable in this codebase's jsdom setup, similar tests already exist for other computed-style assertions), clicks "next" to move to a page with fewer remaining items, and asserts the captured width is IDENTICAL before and after. A test that only reads the source code's intent doesn't count — this needs to actually catch the regression if it recurs, the same way the Step 3 pagination-selection bug's regression test had to actually observe real DOM state.

## What NOT to do

Do not touch `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/` (Step 2, committed). Do not touch `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` (Step 1, committed). Do not touch `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` or anything under `theme/foundation/`. Do not re-litigate the pagination-selection-page fix from the previous rework round (the `useEffect`/`selectedPageStart` logic) — that was independently verified correct twice already, including by a live reviewer-authored test, and must not be touched by this round.

## Verification — run yourself, report exact output

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx
npm run test
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Baselines right now: tsc 0 errors; scoped test file currently 10/10 passing (you're adding at least 1 new test for the width-stability check, and possibly restructuring the Default/KeyboardNavigation story split which doesn't add Vitest tests); full suite 28 files/428 tests before this round; lint 20 problems (4 pre-existing errors, not yours)/16 warnings, exit 1; audit:tokens exactly 4 unacknowledged/22 acknowledged, exit 1 — your changes must add zero new unacknowledged findings (a function-form `baseStyle` with token-driven values inside is fine, same pattern Step 2 already established).

Report back: exactly which files you changed (should be `index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, and `index.test.tsx` — confirm via `git status`), the before/after width measurements from your new regression test (actual numbers, not just "passed"), and confirmation of what `Default`'s play function now does (or that it no longer has one, if you judged that the right call) plus the new story's name and what it asserts.
